Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 39, verses 1–4:

Explanation of the words:

Tanzil al-Kitab (The revelation of the Book): That is, the Qur'an is from Allah.

Al-'Aziz al-Hakim (the Mighty, the Wise): That is, Mighty in His dominion and in His retribution, Wise in His creation and in His management of His creatures.

Mukhlisan lahu al-din (sincere to Him in religion): That is, singling Him out in worship, so you do not associate anyone with His worship.

Lillah al-din al-khalis (To Allah belongs pure religion): That is, to Him alone belongs pure worship; none other than Him shares in that.

Awliya' (protectors/patrons): That is, partners, and they are the idols.

Liyuqarribuna ila Allah zulfa (that they may bring us near to Allah in closeness): That is, bringing us near, and interceding for us with Allah.

Man huwa kadhib kaffar (one who is a liar and a deep disbeliever): That is, a liar, i.e., against Allah, and a disbeliever by worshipping other than Allah, the Most High.

Subhanahu (Glorified is He): That is, exalted above having a son or a partner.

Huwa Allah al-Wahid al-Qahhar (He is Allah, the One, the Subduer): That is, the true object of worship, the One who has no partner in His dominion and authority, the Subduer over His creation.

Meaning of the verses:

The revelation of the Book from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise: He, the Most High, informs that the sending down of the Qur'an was from Him, glorified and exalted, and He is Mighty in His retribution against His enemies and Wise in the management of His creation. It was not from anyone else in any way.

His saying, the Most High, ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth﴾: The Most High informs His Messenger, saying ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book﴾, that is, the magnificent Qur'an, ﴿in truth﴾ in everything it contains and calls to of beliefs, acts of worship and rulings. And upon this, ﴿so worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾, that is, in worship; so do not worship anything alongside Him, for worship is not fitting for anyone else at all. ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs pure religion. And those who take protectors other than Him [say], "We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in closeness."﴾ That is, partners whom they worship and say, "We only worship them that they may bring us near to Allah in closeness and intercede for us with Allah in the fulfilment of our needs." Allah will judge between them concerning that in which they differ with the believing monotheists, and that will be on the Day of Resurrection. He will recompense each, with His justice, according to what they deserve of bounty and honour, or of misery and punishment.

His saying, the Most High, ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a liar and a disbeliever﴾: The Most High informs of the deprivation of certain people from His guidance, namely those who have plunged deeply into corruption, lying about Allah, the Most High, and about His servants, so that lying became a constant attribute of theirs; and they disbelieved and exceeded in disbelief in Allah, His signs, His Messenger and the meeting with Him, so that disbelief became a settled attribute of theirs. This is His practice regarding the servant's deprivation of guidance, so that the decree of Allah concerning their wretchedness and their punishment on the Day of Resurrection may take effect.

His saying, the Most High, ﴿Had Allah desired to take a son﴾, as the polytheists claim, who said the angels are daughters of Allah; and as the Christians said, the Messiah is the son of Allah; and as the Jews said, 'Uzair is the son of Allah. Had Allah wished to have a son, He would have chosen and selected from what He creates whatever He wills, and He would not leave them to attribute a son to Him as a fabrication and a lie against Him. But He, the Most High, is exalted above the attributes of created things and the neediness of creatures, for He is Allah, possessing divinity over all His creation, the One who has no partner in His dominion, authority and rule, the Subduer over all His creation. Glorified is He; there is no god but Him and no lord besides Him.

Guidance from the verses:

1. Affirmation of Muhammadan prophethood.
2. Affirmation of monotheism (tawhid).
3. Refutation of polytheism and denunciation of polytheists.
4. Affirmation of resurrection and recompense on the Day of Judgment.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 39, verses 5–7:

Explanation of the words:

"Khalaqa al-samawati wa al-ard bi al-haqq" (He created the heavens and the earth with truth): that is, so that He may be remembered and thanked, not for play or aimlessness.

"Yukawwiru al-layla 'ala al-nahar" (He wraps the night over the day): that is, He makes one of them enter into the other; when night comes, day departs, and vice versa.

"Wa sakhkhara al-shamsa wa al-qamar" (And He subjected the sun and the moon): that is, He made them subservient, so they continue to revolve in their orbits until the end of life, and through their revolving the interests of the inhabitants of the earth are accomplished.

"Khalaqakum min nafsin wahidah" (He created you from a single soul): it is Adam, peace be upon him.

"Thumma ja'ala minha zawjaha" (Then He made from it its mate): it is Eve, whom God Most High created from the left rib of Adam.

"Wa anzala lakum mina al-an'am" (And He sent down for you of the livestock): that is, He sent down rain, which made vegetation grow, and from it the livestock were created; this is the manner in which they were "sent down."

"Thamaniyata azwaj" (eight mates): that is, two of the camels, two of the cattle, two of the sheep, and two of the goats.

"Yakhluqukum fi buṭuni ummahatikum khalqan min ba'di khalq" (He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation): that is, stages, one stage after another: a drop (nutfah), then a clot (‘alaqah), then a lump of flesh (mudghah).

"Fi zulumatin thalath" (in three darknesses): that is, the darkness of the belly, the darkness of the womb, and the darkness of the placenta.

"Wa la taziru waziratun wizra ukhra" (And no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another): that is, no soul burdened with sin bears the sin of another soul.

"Innahu 'alimun bidhat al-sudur" (Indeed He is Knowing of what is within the breasts): that is, what a person conceals in his chest and what he keeps secret in his inner self.

Meaning of the verses:

These noble verses establish monotheism by mentioning the proofs and evidences that leave no room for doubt in the minds of people of intellect. God Most High says in verse [5]: ﴿He created the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, He brought them into existence as a creation without any prior model, and He created them with truth, for lofty and noble ends, not for falsehood and aimlessness; among those ends is that He be worshipped therein, remembered and thanked. His saying ﴿He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night﴾ means that He covers one with the other, concealing and veiling it, as if He wound it around and covered it with it. This is a second proof, the first being the proof of the creation of the heavens and the earth, and a third proof is in His saying ﴿And He subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a term appointed﴾, revolving in their orbits until the Hour arrives; and in that there are benefits and interests for the servants beyond measure, among them knowing the number of years and calculation. His saying ﴿Unquestionably, He is the Mighty, the Forgiving﴾ is a declaration and warning that He is Mighty in His seizing and His retribution against His enemies, and Forgiving toward His servants who turn to Him in repentance.

His saying in verse [6] ﴿He created you from a single soul﴾ refers to Adam, peace be upon him. It is authentically reported that when God created Adam, He wiped over his back and brought forth from it his offspring and made them bear witness concerning themselves. For this reason the particle "thumma" (then) is used in ﴿He created you from a single soul, then He made from it its mate﴾, meaning: after He wiped over Adam's back, brought forth his offspring from his back, and made them bear witness concerning themselves, He created Eve from his left rib. This is another proof, found in His saying ﴿And He sent down for you of the livestock﴾, namely the camels, the cattle and the sheep and goats, male and female; the male is a mate and the female is a mate, so they are eight mates. It is possible that the origin of these livestock was sent down from the heaven, just as Adam and Eve were sent down from heaven; and it is possible that He sent down water, so vegetation grew and these livestock came into being from it. Thus the origin is the sending down from heaven, and the gradual process of creation took place on the earth.

A fourth proof is in His saying ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation﴾, that is: a drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then bones, then We clothe the bones with flesh; then he is a complete human being. His saying ﴿in three darknesses﴾ refers to the darkness of the mother's belly, then the darkness of the womb, then the darkness of the placenta, which is a membrane that forms around the child, and which in animals is called al-salaa.

After mentioning these proofs He said ﴿That is God, your Lord﴾, that is, your Creator and your true object of worship, ﴿to Him belongs the dominion; there is no god but Him﴾, that is, there is no one worthy of worship except Him, since worship is fitting only for Him, ﴿so how are you turned away?﴾, that is, how are you turned away from the truth to falsehood, and from guidance to misguidance? Indeed your situation is strange.

His saying in verse [7] ﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed God is Independent of you﴾, that is, after He explained through decisive proofs the obligation of faith in Him and the obligation of worshipping Him, and that He is the true Lord and the true God, He informed His servants that their disbelief in Him does not harm Him at all, because He is Independent of them and of all His creation. Yet, out of His mercy toward His servants, He does not approve disbelief for them, because of the misery and loss it causes them; just as, if they believe and give thanks, He approves it for them, rewarding them with the best reward and recompensing them with the best recompense. His saying ﴿and no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another﴾ is a manifestation of His justice among His servants: no soul burdened with sin, that is, with a wrong, bears the sin of another soul; rather every soul bears its own burden and alone undergoes its consequences and results. His saying ﴿Then to your Lord is your return﴾, that is, after death, ﴿then He will inform you of what you used to do﴾, that is, He will tell you of your deeds, hidden and manifest, small and great, ﴿Indeed He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾, beyond what was an outward action and not inward, and He will recompense you for good with its like and for evil with its like. So this is your true Lord and your truthful God; believe in Him, affirm His oneness, do not associate anything with Him, obey Him and do not disobey Him, and you will be saved and made happy in this world and the Hereafter. And none perishes before God except one who is destined to perish.

Guidance of the verses:

1- The demonstration of God's signs in the cosmos and their presentation as proofs of monotheism.

2- The demonstration of God's bounty upon His servants in their creation and provision.

3- The demonstration that disbelief is more strange than belief, for the proofs of belief are beyond counting, whereas for disbelief there is no proof at all; yet most people are disbelievers.

4- The demonstration of God's independence from His creation and the creation's dependence upon Him.

5- The demonstration of God's justice on the Day of Resurrection and its establishment.

6- The demonstration of the comprehensiveness of God's knowledge of creation and His knowledge of their deeds and states, outward and inward.

1- The demonstration of God's signs in the cosmos and their presentation as proofs of monotheism.

2- The demonstration of God's bounty upon His servants in their creation and provision.

3- The demonstration that disbelief is more strange than belief, for the proofs of belief are beyond counting, whereas for disbelief there is no proof at all; yet most people are disbelievers.

4- The demonstration of God's independence from His creation and the creation's dependence upon Him.

5- The demonstration of God's justice on the Day of Resurrection and its establishment.

6- The demonstration of the comprehensiveness of God's knowledge of creation and His knowledge of their deeds and states, outward and inward.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 39, verses 5–7:

Explanation of the words:

"Khalaqa al-samawati wa al-ard bi al-haqq" (He created the heavens and the earth with truth): that is, so that He may be remembered and thanked, not for play or aimlessness.

"Yukawwiru al-layla 'ala al-nahar" (He wraps the night over the day): that is, He makes one of them enter into the other; when night comes, day departs, and vice versa.

"Wa sakhkhara al-shamsa wa al-qamar" (And He subjected the sun and the moon): that is, He made them subservient, so they continue to revolve in their orbits until the end of life, and through their revolving the interests of the inhabitants of the earth are accomplished.

"Khalaqakum min nafsin wahidah" (He created you from a single soul): it is Adam, peace be upon him.

"Thumma ja'ala minha zawjaha" (Then He made from it its mate): it is Eve, whom God Most High created from the left rib of Adam.

"Wa anzala lakum mina al-an'am" (And He sent down for you of the livestock): that is, He sent down rain, which made vegetation grow, and from it the livestock were created; this is the manner in which they were "sent down."

"Thamaniyata azwaj" (eight mates): that is, two of the camels, two of the cattle, two of the sheep, and two of the goats.

"Yakhluqukum fi buṭuni ummahatikum khalqan min ba'di khalq" (He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation): that is, stages, one stage after another: a drop (nutfah), then a clot (‘alaqah), then a lump of flesh (mudghah).

"Fi zulumatin thalath" (in three darknesses): that is, the darkness of the belly, the darkness of the womb, and the darkness of the placenta.

"Wa la taziru waziratun wizra ukhra" (And no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another): that is, no soul burdened with sin bears the sin of another soul.

"Innahu 'alimun bidhat al-sudur" (Indeed He is Knowing of what is within the breasts): that is, what a person conceals in his chest and what he keeps secret in his inner self.

Meaning of the verses:

These noble verses establish monotheism by mentioning the proofs and evidences that leave no room for doubt in the minds of people of intellect. God Most High says in verse [5]: ﴿He created the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, He brought them into existence as a creation without any prior model, and He created them with truth, for lofty and noble ends, not for falsehood and aimlessness; among those ends is that He be worshipped therein, remembered and thanked. His saying ﴿He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night﴾ means that He covers one with the other, concealing and veiling it, as if He wound it around and covered it with it. This is a second proof, the first being the proof of the creation of the heavens and the earth, and a third proof is in His saying ﴿And He subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a term appointed﴾, revolving in their orbits until the Hour arrives; and in that there are benefits and interests for the servants beyond measure, among them knowing the number of years and calculation. His saying ﴿Unquestionably, He is the Mighty, the Forgiving﴾ is a declaration and warning that He is Mighty in His seizing and His retribution against His enemies, and Forgiving toward His servants who turn to Him in repentance.

His saying in verse [6] ﴿He created you from a single soul﴾ refers to Adam, peace be upon him. It is authentically reported that when God created Adam, He wiped over his back and brought forth from it his offspring and made them bear witness concerning themselves. For this reason the particle "thumma" (then) is used in ﴿He created you from a single soul, then He made from it its mate﴾, meaning: after He wiped over Adam's back, brought forth his offspring from his back, and made them bear witness concerning themselves, He created Eve from his left rib. This is another proof, found in His saying ﴿And He sent down for you of the livestock﴾, namely the camels, the cattle and the sheep and goats, male and female; the male is a mate and the female is a mate, so they are eight mates. It is possible that the origin of these livestock was sent down from the heaven, just as Adam and Eve were sent down from heaven; and it is possible that He sent down water, so vegetation grew and these livestock came into being from it. Thus the origin is the sending down from heaven, and the gradual process of creation took place on the earth.

A fourth proof is in His saying ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation﴾, that is: a drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then bones, then We clothe the bones with flesh; then he is a complete human being. 2- The demonstration of God's bounty upon His servants in their creation and provision.

3- The demonstration that disbelief is more strange than belief, for the proofs of belief are beyond counting, whereas for disbelief there is no proof at all; yet most people are disbelievers.

4- The demonstration of God's independence from His creation and the creation's dependence upon Him.

5- The demonstration of God's justice on the Day of Resurrection and its establishment.

6- The demonstration of the comprehensiveness of God's knowledge of creation and His knowledge of their deeds and states, outward and inward.

**Explanation of the Words (Sharh al-Kalimat):**

*Wa-idha massa al-insana*: "al-insan" means the polytheist (al-mushrik).

*Darr*: means sickness, or fear of drowning and the like, any hardship one cannot repel.

*Da'a rabbahu muniban ilayh*: means he asked his Lord to remove the harm that had befallen him, turning back to Him and turning away from anyone else.

*Idha khawwalahu ni'matan minh*: means He gave him a blessing from Himself, by removing the harm he had suffered.

*Nasiya ma kana yad'u ilayhi min qabl*: means he abandoned what he had earlier humbly called upon, which was Allah, glorified and exalted is He.

*Wa ja'ala lillahi andadan*: means partners (shuraka').

*Li-yudilla 'an sabilih*: means to lead astray himself and others from Islam.

*Qul tamatta' bikufrika qalilan*: means, say, O our Prophet, to this disbelieving, misguided and misleading person, as a threat: enjoy your disbelief for the remainder of your term.

*Innaka min ashab al-nar*: means its people, those who are deserving of it because of the corruption of their souls and the darkness of their spirits.

*Qanit anaa' al-layl*: means obedient to Allah during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing in prayer.

*Innama yatadhakkaru ulu al-albab*: means those who are admonished by the verses they hear are people of luminous intellects.

**Meaning of the Verses (Ma'na al-Ayat):**

The context continues to establish *tawhid* (the oneness of Allah) and refute *tandid* (setting up rivals to Allah). Allah, the Exalted, says, informing about the state of the polytheist who takes rivals to his Lord and worships them alongside Him: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance﴾, meaning he asks his Lord, returning to Him and raising his hands to Him, saying, "O my Lord! O my Lord!", seeking the relief of what afflicts him and the removal of what has befallen him. ﴿Then when He bestows upon him a favor from Himself, he forgets what he had called upon Him for before﴾, meaning that when Allah relieves his distress and rescues him, he abandons the supplication to Allah and turns to worshipping other than Allah. ﴿And he sets up rivals to Allah﴾, meaning partners, ﴿to mislead [others] from His way﴾, meaning he misleads himself and others.

Here Allah commanded His Messenger to say to him on Allah's behalf: say, O our Messenger, to this disbelieving polytheist, "Enjoy your disbelief for a little while," meaning for the remainder of your life, "indeed you are among the companions of the Fire." Thus his Lord threatened him and warned him of the consequence of associating partners with Allah and setting up rivals, so that perhaps he would desist, repent sincerely, and return to Allah with a good and beautiful return. This is what the first verse [8] indicates.

As for the second verse [9], Allah says: ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient﴾, meaning obedient to Allah and His Messenger in their commands and prohibitions, ﴿during the hours of the night﴾, meaning the hours of the night, you see him prostrating in his prayer or standing reciting the verses of Allah in his prayer, and at the same time he fears the punishment of the Hereafter and asks Allah, the Exalted, to protect him from it, and hopes for the mercy of his Lord, which is Paradise, that Allah make him among its people. Is this better, or that disbeliever to whom it was said, "Enjoy your disbelief for a little while; indeed you are among the companions of the Fire"? The answer is known to people of understanding.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Are those who know equal to those who do not know?﴾, [meaning] those who know what Allah loves and what He dislikes, and who act to do what Allah loves, seeking nearness to Him, and to abandon what He dislikes, seeking His love. Are these who act equal to those who do not know what He loves and what He dislikes, and who wander in misguidance like the wandering of the ignorant? The answer is: they are not equal. Only those of sound and superior intellect are admonished by this divine guidance and lordly instruction, namely the people of understanding (ulu al-albab), that is, the sound and sensible minds.

**Guidance from the Verses (Hidayat al-Ayat):**

Among the guidance of these verses:

1. The affirmation of *tawhid* and the refutation of *shirk* (association) and *tandid* (setting up rivals).

2. The revelation of the inner nature of man before he believes and submits: that he is a contradictory being with no good in him and no right guidance, so he is not guided nor perfected except through faith and *tawhid*.

3. Good news to those who stray from the way of Allah and lead others astray from it: the Fire.

4. A comparison between the obedient devotee and the disobedient one who misleads and is plainly astray, and between the one who knows and the one who does not know; and the affirmation of the superiority of the obedient believer over the disobedient disbeliever, and the superiority of one who knows Allah and what He loves and dislikes over one who does not.

5. The excellence of the knowledgeable over the ignorant because of his acting upon his knowledge; were it not for acting on knowledge, the two would be equal in baseness and degradation.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 39, verses 10–16:

Explanation of the words:

اتقوا ربكم (ittaqū rabbakum): i.e., make between yourselves and His punishment a shield through faith and God-consciousness (taqwa).

للذين أحسنوا (lilladhīna aḥsanū): i.e., those who did good in worship.

حسنة (ḥasanah): i.e., Paradise.

أرض الله واسعة (arḍu llāhi wāsi'ah): i.e., so emigrate within it so that you may be able to worship God if you are prevented from doing so in your homelands.

أُمرت (umirtu): i.e., my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded me.

مخلصا له الدين (mukhliṣan lahu l-dīn): i.e., singling Him out alone for worship.

أول المسلمين (awwal al-muslimīn): i.e., the first to submit in this community, surrendering to God through worship and sincerity toward Him in it.

عذاب يوم عظيم ('adhāba yawmin 'aẓīm): i.e., the punishment of the Day of Resurrection.

قل (qul): i.e., O our Messenger, to the polytheists.

الله أعبد (Allāha a'budu): i.e., I do not worship along with Him any other.

مخلصا له ديني (mukhliṣan lahu dīnī): i.e., singling Him out alone for my obedience and submission.

فاعبدوا ما شئتم (fa-'budū mā shi'tum): i.e., if you, O polytheists, refuse to worship God alone, then worship whatever you wish of the idols, for you are indeed losers.

خسروا أنفسهم (khasirū anfusahum): i.e., they deprived themselves of Paradise and made themselves abide forever in the Fire.

وأهليهم (wa-ahlīhim): i.e., the wide-eyed maidens (ḥūr 'īn) who would have been theirs in Paradise had they believed and been God-conscious by performing acts of obedience and abstaining from what is forbidden.

ظلل من النار (ẓulalun min al-nār): i.e., smoke, flame and heat from above them and from below them.

ذلك (dhālika): i.e., the aforementioned punishment of the Fire.

يا عباد فاتقون (yā 'ibādi fa-ttaqūn): i.e., O you whom I created, provided for, and own, and what they possess; therefore, be God-conscious of Me through faith and taqwa.

Meaning of the verses:

These five verses contain divine directives and guidance for the believers and for the Messenger ﷺ. In the first verse [10], God commands His Messenger to tell the believers, "Be God-conscious of your Lord," i.e., make between yourselves and the punishment of God a shield, by obeying Him and obeying His Messenger. He informs them, explaining His command to them to be God-conscious, that for those who perform the obedience required of them is Paradise. He also informs them that if they are unable to obey among the polytheists, then they should emigrate to a land where they can obey God and His Messenger. So He says, ﴿And the earth of God is spacious﴾, i.e., so emigrate within it, and He encourages them to emigrate for the sake of obedience, saying, ﴿Only the patient will be given their reward without account﴾, i.e., those who endure estrangement and emigration for the sake of obedience to God and the Messenger, ﴿their reward without account﴾, i.e., without measure, without weighing, and without counting, because it is beyond all that.

In the second [11] and third [12] verses, God commands His Messenger, addressing him, to tell the people, ﴿Indeed I have been commanded﴾, i.e., my Lord commanded me to worship God with belief, speech and action, doing what He commands me and abstaining from what He forbids me, ﴿sincere to Him in religion﴾, so that I do not associate anyone with God in His religion, i.e., in His worship. And He commanded me to be ﴿the first of the Muslims﴾ in this community, i.e., the first to submit, with his heart and his outward and inward limbs, to God the Exalted.

In the fourth [13] and fifth [14] verses, God the Exalted commands His Messenger to tell the polytheists, "Indeed I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great Day," and He commands him to say, ﴿God I worship﴾, i.e., God alone, without partner, I worship, while being sincere to Him in my religion. As for you, O polytheists, if you refuse monotheism, then worship whatever you wish of the deities other than Him. And He commands him to tell them that the truly losers are not those who lose their worldly life, losing home, camel, wealth, family or children; rather, they are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection, by being made to abide forever in the Fire, and by not reaching the wide-eyed maidens prepared for them in Paradise had they believed and been God-conscious.

﴿Indeed, that is the manifest loss.﴾ Then He clarifies that loss by the following state: that for them, while they are in the Fire, there are ﴿layers of fire above them and layers below them﴾, i.e., above them a layer and below them another, all of them smoke, flame and heat. Finally, God the Exalted says, ﴿That﴾, i.e., the aforementioned loss and the torment of the layers, with which God causes His believing servants to fear, so that they may persevere in their obedience and their patience upon it, and thus be saved from the Fire and attain the Gardens. His saying "O My servants, so fear Me" means: O My believing servants, so fear Me and do not disobey, and God warns them of Himself; and God is Kind to His servants.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Demonstration of God's care for His Messenger and the believers, as He guided them to what perfects and makes them happy.

2- The obligation of God-consciousness and of patience over harm in that.

3- Affirmation of monotheism by worshipping God alone.

4- The excellence of Islam and the nobility of Muslims.

5- Affirmation of resurrection and recompense, with an explanation of some of the terrors of the Hereafter and the punishment of the Fire therein.

6- Every loss in this world, when measured against the loss of the Hereafter, is never considered a loss at all.

فاعبدوا ما شئتم (fa-'budū mā shi'tum): i.e., if you, O polytheists, refuse to worship God alone, then worship whatever you wish of the idols, for you are indeed losers.

خسروا أنفسهم (khasirū anfusahum): i.e., they deprived themselves of Paradise and made themselves abide forever in the Fire.

وأهليهم (wa-ahlīhim): i.e., the wide-eyed maidens (ḥūr 'īn) who would have been theirs in Paradise had they believed and been God-conscious by performing acts of obedience and abstaining from what is forbidden.

ظلل من النار (ẓulalun min al-nār): i.e., smoke, flame and heat from above them and from below them.

ذلك (dhālika): i.e., the aforementioned punishment of the Fire.

يا عباد فاتقون (yā 'ibādi fa-ttaqūn): i.e., O you whom I created, provided for, and own, and what they possess; therefore, be God-conscious of Me through faith and taqwa.

Meaning of the verses:

These five verses contain divine directives and guidance for the believers and for the Messenger ﷺ. In the first verse [10], God commands His Messenger to tell the believers, "Be God-conscious of your Lord," i.e., make between yourselves and the punishment of God a shield, by obeying Him and obeying His Messenger. He informs them, explaining His command to them to be God-conscious, that for those who perform the obedience required of them is Paradise. He also informs them that if they are unable to obey among the polytheists, then they should emigrate to a land where they can obey God and His Messenger. So He says, ﴿And the earth of God is spacious﴾, i.e., so emigrate within it, and He encourages them to emigrate for the sake of obedience, saying, ﴿Only the patient will be given their reward without account﴾, i.e., those who endure estrangement and emigration for the sake of obedience to God and the Messenger, ﴿their reward without account﴾, i.e., without measure, without weighing, and without counting, because it is beyond all that.

In the second [11] and third [12] verses, God commands His Messenger, addressing him, to tell the people, ﴿Indeed I have been commanded﴾, i.e., my Lord commanded me to worship God with belief, speech and action, doing what He commands me and abstaining from what He forbids me, ﴿sincere to Him in religion﴾, so that I do not associate anyone with God in His religion, i.e., in His worship. And He commanded me to be ﴿the first of the Muslims﴾ in this community, i.e., the first to submit, with his heart and his outward and inward limbs, to God the Exalted.

In the fourth [13] and fifth [14] verses, God the Exalted commands His Messenger to tell the polytheists, "Indeed I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great Day," and He commands him to say, ﴿God I worship﴾, i.e., God alone, without partner, I worship, while being sincere to Him in my religion. As for you, O polytheists, if you refuse monotheism, then worship whatever you wish of the deities other than Him. And He commands him to tell them that the truly losers are not those who lose their worldly life, losing home, camel, wealth, family or children; rather, they are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection, by being made to abide forever in the Fire, and by not reaching the wide-eyed maidens prepared for them in Paradise had they believed and been God-conscious.

﴿Indeed, that is the manifest loss.﴾ Then He clarifies that loss by the following state: that for them, while they are in the Fire, there are ﴿layers of fire above them and layers below them﴾, i.e., above them a layer and below them another, all of them smoke, flame and heat. Finally, God the Exalted says, ﴿That﴾, i.e., the aforementioned loss and the torment of the layers, with which God causes His believing servants to fear, so that they may persevere in their obedience and their patience upon it, and thus be saved from the Fire and attain the Gardens. His saying "O My servants, so fear Me" means: O My believing servants, so fear Me and do not disobey, and God warns them of Himself; and God is Kind to His servants.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Demonstration of God's care for His Messenger and the believers, as He guided them to what perfects and makes them happy.

2- The obligation of God-consciousness and of patience over harm in that.

3- Affirmation of monotheism by worshipping God alone.

4- The excellence of Islam and the nobility of Muslims.

5- Affirmation of resurrection and recompense, with an explanation of some of the terrors of the Hereafter and the punishment of the Fire therein.

6- Every loss in this world, when measured against the loss of the Hereafter, is never considered a loss at all.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 39, verses 17–20:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Those who avoid the Taghut (tāghūt, every object of worship besides Allah) from worshipping them⦆: that is, they abandoned the worship of idols and other things that are worshipped besides Allah.

﴿And turn penitently to Allah⦆: that is, by believing in Him, worshipping Him, and making Him one in that worship.

﴿For them is good news⦆: that is, of Paradise at the time of death, in the grave, and at rising from the graves.

﴿Then they follow the best of it⦆: that is, the most complete, most perfect, and closest to the pleasure of Allah, the Exalted.

﴿Those of understanding (ulū al-albāb)⦆: that is, those with sound intellects.

﴿Then is he against whom the word of punishment has come into effect⦆: that is, punishment has become due for him by the saying of Allah, the Exalted, "I will surely fill Hell."

﴿Would you, then, save one who is in the Fire?⦆: that is, rescue him from it and bring him out of its punishment.

﴿But those who fear their Lord⦆: that is, they feared Him, so they believed in Him and obeyed Him, making Him one in that.

﴿Under them rivers flow⦆: that is, through their palaces and trees.

﴿The promise of Allah⦆: that is, Allah promised them a promise, and He fulfills it for them.

Meaning of the verses:

When the Exalted mentioned the condition of the people of the Fire, from among the worshippers of idols, and that for them there are canopies of Fire above them and canopies beneath them, He mentioned the condition of those who avoided those taghuts and did not worship them, and what He prepared for them of lasting bliss. Thus He combined warning and encouragement, which is required for guiding and reforming mankind. So He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And those who avoided the Taghut⦆, that is, from worshipping them, and they are the idols and everything the Shaytan made appealing to worship and called people to worship. And they added to avoiding the Taghut the turning penitently to Allah, the Exalted, by worshipping Him and making Him one in that. These are the ones for whom there is good news, which is in the Book of Allah and on the tongue of the Messenger of Allah, and they will see it at the descent of death, in the grave, at the gathering, and all of this is in the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ). And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So give good tidings to My servants who listen to the Word and follow the best of it⦆. The Exalted commands His Messenger to give good news to a category of His servants with what He gave good news to those who avoided the Taghut from worshipping them and turned penitently to Allah. They are those who listen to speech from its speaker and follow the best of what they hear, and they leave both its good and its bad. These have lofty aspirations, souls longing for goodness and perfection, and noble natures, so they deserved the good news on the tongue of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the beautiful praise of the Lord of the worlds, when He said about them: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, and those are the people of understanding⦆. So it is sufficient perfection for them that Allah praised them. O Allah, make me among them, and grant that to whoever asks for it for me and for himself. And His saying: ﴿Then is he against whom the word of punishment has come into effect⦆, that is, punishment became due for him by decree and destiny, so he excessively persisted in disbelief, wrongdoing, criminality and transgression, like Abu Jahl and al-As ibn Wa'il, so his sins encompassed him and he became one of the companions of the Fire. Can you, O Messenger, save him from the Fire and rescue him from it? The answer is no. So then ease your soul, leave them to their affair, and to what they were created for and what was decreed upon them. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿But those who feared their Lord⦆, who believed and did righteous deeds, for them are upper chambers in Paradise, above which are upper chambers, that is the high rooms built above the room, ﴿under them rivers flow⦆, beneath the palaces and trees, rivers of water, milk, honey and wine.

And His saying: ﴿The promise of Allah⦆, that is, Allah promised them with it a true promise, and He fulfills it for them, since He, the Exalted, does not break the promise.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The honour of Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari and Salman al-Farisi, for this verse concerns them, as they rejected the worship of the taghut in the Jahiliyyah before Islam, then turned penitently to their Lord, so the verse was true of them.

2- The virtue of people of discernment, awareness and understanding, who distinguish between what they hear, following the best and leaving what is lesser of good and bad.

3- An announcement from Allah, the Exalted, that whoever has been destined for the Fire from eternity cannot be guided, however much the caller strives to guide and reform him.

4- An explanation of what Allah, the Exalted, has prepared for the people of faith and piety of the bliss of Paradise and Allah's honouring of its people.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 39, verses 21–23:

Explanation of the words:

﴿فَسَلَكَهُ يَنَابِيعَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ (fa-salakahu yanabee'a fi al-ardh): He caused it to enter the earth, so that it became flowing beneath it, springing forth from it, and thus became springs.

﴿مُّخْتَلِفاً أَلْوَانُهُ﴾ (mukhtalifan alwanuhu): i.e., of various colors, between green, white, red and yellow, and of various kinds: wheat, barley and sorghum.

﴿ثُمَّ يَهِيجُ فَتَرَاهُ مُصْفَرّاً﴾ (thumma yahiju fataraahu musfarran): i.e., it dries up, so that you, O beholder, see it yellow after being green.

﴿ثُمَّ يَجْعَلُهُ حُطَاماً﴾ (thumma yaj'aluhu hutaman): i.e., crumbled into pieces, broken.

﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَذِكْرَىٰ﴾ (inna fi dhalika ladhikra): i.e., indeed in that which has been mentioned, from the sending down of water until it becomes crumbled debris, there is a reminder.

﴿أَفَمَن شَرَحَ ٱللَّهُ صَدْرَهُ لِلإِسْلَامِ﴾ (afaman sharaha Allahu sadrahu lil-Islam): i.e., one who is guided by it is like one whom God has not expanded his breast for guidance and so is not guided?

﴿فَهُوَ عَلَىٰ نُورٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِ﴾ (fahuwa ala nurin min rabbih): i.e., he lives his life upon a light from his Lord, which is the knowledge of God and His laws.

﴿فَوَيْلٌ لِّلْقَاسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُم مِّن ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ (fa-wayl lil-qasiyati qulubuhum min dhikri Allah): Woe (wayl) is a word of punishment for those whose hearts are hard against accepting the Qur'an, so they do not believe in it and do not act upon what is in it.

﴿أَحْسَنَ ٱلْحَدِيثِ كِتَاباً﴾ (ahsana al-hadithi kitaban): it is the Noble Qur'an.

﴿مُّتَشَابِهاً﴾ (mutashabihan): i.e., some of it resembles other parts in arrangement, beauty and soundness of meanings.

﴿مَّثَانِيَ﴾ (mathani): i.e., the promise and the threat are repeated in it, as in the narratives and the rulings.

﴿تَقْشَعِرُّ مِنْهُ جُلُودُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ﴾ (taqshaʿirru minhu julud alladhina yakhshawna rabbahum): i.e., the skins of those who fear their Lord tremble from it, and this is at the mention of His threat.

﴿ثُمَّ تَلِينُ جُلُودُهُمْ وَقُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ (thumma talinu julūduhum wa qulūbuhum): i.e., they become calm and soft.

﴿إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ (ila dhikri Allah): i.e., at the mention of His promise to the people of faith and piety of Paradise and its everlasting bliss.

Meaning of the verses:

Allah's words ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾ ("Have you not seen"): This noble verse establishes tawhid (the oneness of God), resurrection and recompense by mentioning the manifestations of divine power and knowledge. These two imply first the existence of God, then the obligation to believe in Him and in meeting Him. So for such a person there is no guide after Allah, ever.

Lessons of the verses:

From the lessons of these verses:

1- The manifestations of divine knowledge and power, which necessitate belief in Him, His Messenger, and meeting Him.

2- The explanation that hearts are of two kinds: a heart that is receptive to guidance and another that is not.

3- The explanation that the Qur'an is the best speech a believer can relate, since its reports are all true and its rulings all just.

4- The virtue of those who fear Allah, for they are the ones who are moved by hearing the Qur'an: their skins tremble at hearing its threat, and their hearts and skins soften at hearing its promise.

Word Explanations (Sharh al-Kalimat):

Afaman yattaqi bi-wajhihi su'a al-'adhab: i.e., he receives the punishment with his face, having nothing to shield him from it, unlike one who is secure.

Su' al-'adhab: its harshest and most severe form.

Wa-qila lil-zalimin: i.e., the polytheists in Hell.

Dhuqu ma kuntum taksibun: i.e., the recompense of your earning of evil and corruption.

Kadhdhaba alladhina min qablihim: i.e., those before the people of Makkah.

Fa-ataahum al-'adhab min haythu la yash'urun: i.e., from a direction they did not know it would come from, or from a direction that never occurred to them.

Fa-adhaqahum Allah 'adhab al-khizy: i.e., disfigurement (maskh), humiliation and degradation.

Wa-la-'adhab al-akhirati akbar law kanu ya'lamun: i.e., had they known that, they would not have denied or disbelieved.

Meaning of the Verses (Ma'na al-Ayat):

The noble context continues to establish the Resurrection and recompense. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Is one who shields his face from the terrible punishment on the Day of Resurrection—since he has nothing to protect himself with, for his hands are chained to his neck, so he receives the punishment with his face, the most noble of his limbs—like one who is safe from punishment and enters Paradise?﴾ The answer is: they are not equal. And His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And it will be said to the wrongdoers﴾, meaning the polytheists, who are in the Fire, the guardians of Hell will say to them, in rebuke and reproach: ﴿Taste what you used to earn﴾ of works of polytheism and sins. This is its recompense, so taste it, a painful punishment. And His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Those before them denied﴾, meaning nations and peoples before the people of Makkah denied their messengers, so Allah made them taste disgrace in the life of this world, such as humiliation, disfigurement, killing, captivity and enslavement. The punishment of the Hereafter is greater than the punishment of this world, and they are heading toward it without doubt. And His saying, ﴿if only they knew﴾, meaning, if they had known of it with certainty of knowledge, they would not have denied their messengers nor disbelieved in their Lord. Thus they perished through their ignorance.

Guidance from the Verses (Hidayat al-Ayat):

From the guidance of these verses:

1. Establishing the Resurrection and recompense by mentioning some of the conditions of the Day of Resurrection.
2. A warning to Quraysh for their persistence in denying the Messenger and what he brought them of Islam.
3. Punishment for denial and sins, including both worldly and otherworldly punishment.
4. If people knew the punishment of the Hereafter with certainty, they would not have denied, disbelieved or wronged. Ignorance is always the cause of ruin and wretchedness.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 39, verses 27–31:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And We have certainly presented to the people in this Qur'an every kind of example﴾: that is, We have made for the Arabs, in this Qur'an, every kind of example from the earlier nations.

﴿That they may be reminded﴾: that is, that they may take heed and be restrained from what they are in of shirk (associating partners with God) and denial, towards faith and tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness).

﴿An Arabic Qur'an, without any crookedness﴾: that is, the example made is an Arabic Qur'an, free of ambiguity and contradiction, so they have no excuse for failing to understand it, to grasp its meaning and to comprehend its purpose.

﴿Quarrelling partners (mutashakisun)﴾: that is, quarrelling with one another because of their bad characters.

﴿A man belonging wholly to one man (salaman)﴾: that is, purely and entirely belonging to a man in whom no one else has a share.

﴿Are the two equal in comparison?﴾: The answer is no. The first is in toil and bewilderment, while the second is in ease and tranquillity of mind.

﴿Praise be to God﴾: that is, for the manifestation of the truth and the nullity of falsehood.

﴿You will surely die﴾: that is, you are decreed to die at its appointed time.

﴿And they too will surely die﴾: that is, likewise they are judged to die when their appointed terms come to an end.

﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, you will dispute﴾: that is, you will be brought to God in the court of final judgment, and God will judge between you.

﴿About what you used to dispute﴾: that is, concerning shirk, tawhid, faith and denial.

Explanation of the verses:

The words of the Most High, ﴿And We have certainly presented to the people in this Qur'an every kind of example﴾, inform us of the favour Allah bestowed upon the Arabs for their guidance, in that He placed for them in the noble Qur'an examples of the earlier nations in their faith and denial, their righteousness and corruption, their salvation and loss, all of this in an Arabic Qur'an without crookedness, meaning without ambiguity, obscurity or contradiction. He did this for them so that they may be reminded, that is, that they may take heed, believe and affirm God's oneness, and thereby be saved from punishment and attain felicity. And the words of the Most High, ﴿God presents an example: a man with partners quarrelling, and a man belonging wholly to one man. Are the two equal in comparison?﴾, to the end of the verse, this is one of the examples which God presented to people so that they may be reminded. It is an example of the polytheist who worships several gods, and the monotheist who worships none but God. The polytheist is like a man owned by a number of men with fierce characters and harsh temperaments; they quarrel over him, this one saying to him "come here," the other saying "sit down," and the third saying "stand up," so he is perplexed about his affair, with no ease of body and no ease of conscience and soul. The monotheist is like a man belonging purely and wholly to one man, whose commander and prohibiter is one. "Are the two equal?" means: are the two men equal? The answer is no, since between them lies the difference between freedom and servitude, and greater still. And the words of the Most High, ﴿Praise be to God﴾, mean that all good praise and great thanks belong to God, the Lord who is one and the God who is one, with no god besides Him and no lord other than Him. And His words, ﴿But most of them do not know﴾, mean: but most of the polytheists do not know that the two men are not equal, and that is due to their ignorance and corrupted minds.

His words, ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die﴾, were revealed when the polytheists were slow to see the Messenger ﷺ die, meaning: there is no gloating over death. "You will die, O our Messenger, and they will die." And His words, ﴿Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, you will dispute﴾, mean: believer and disbeliever, strong and weak, all of you will stand before God, and He will judge between you concerning what you used to dispute, both matters of religion and matters of worldly life together.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The legitimacy of presenting examples to greatly enhance understanding and guidance for one who is to be guided.

2- An illustration of the example of the polytheist and the monotheist: the polytheist is in bewilderment and toil, while the monotheist is in ease and tranquillity of mind.

3- Affirmation that every soul shall taste death.

4- An indication that there will be a dispute on the Day of Resurrection, in which God will judge with truth, for He is the Truth.

﴿Are the two equal in comparison?﴾: The answer is no. The first is in toil and bewilderment, while the second is in ease and tranquillity of mind.

﴿Praise be to God﴾: that is, for the manifestation of the truth and the nullity of falsehood.

﴿You will surely die﴾: that is, you are decreed to die at its appointed time.

﴿And they too will surely die﴾: that is, likewise they are judged to die when their appointed terms come to an end.

﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, you will dispute﴾: that is, you will be brought to God in the court of final judgment, and God will judge between you.

﴿About what you used to dispute﴾: that is, concerning shirk, tawhid, faith and denial.

Explanation of the verses:

The words of the Most High, ﴿And We have certainly presented to the people in this Qur'an every kind of example﴾, inform us of the favour Allah bestowed upon the Arabs for their guidance, in that He placed for them in the noble Qur'an examples of the earlier nations in their faith and denial, their righteousness and corruption, their salvation and loss, all of this in an Arabic Qur'an without crookedness, meaning without ambiguity, obscurity or contradiction. He did this for them so that they may be reminded, that is, that they may take heed, believe and affirm God's oneness, and thereby be saved from punishment and attain felicity. And the words of the Most High, ﴿God presents an example: a man with partners quarrelling, and a man belonging wholly to one man. Are the two equal in comparison?﴾, to the end of the verse, this is one of the examples which God presented to people so that they may be reminded. It is an example of the polytheist who worships several gods, and the monotheist who worships none but God. The polytheist is like a man owned by a number of men with fierce characters and harsh temperaments; they quarrel over him, this one saying to him "come here," the other saying "sit down," and the third saying "stand up," so he is perplexed about his affair, with no ease of body and no ease of conscience and soul. The monotheist is like a man belonging purely and wholly to one man, whose commander and prohibiter is one. "Are the two equal?" means: are the two men equal? The answer is no, since between them lies the difference between freedom and servitude, and greater still. And the words of the Most High, ﴿Praise be to God﴾, mean that all good praise and great thanks belong to God, the Lord who is one and the God who is one, with no god besides Him and no lord other than Him. And His words, ﴿But most of them do not know﴾, mean: but most of the polytheists do not know that the two men are not equal, and that is due to their ignorance and corrupted minds.

His words, ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die﴾, were revealed when the polytheists were slow to see the Messenger ﷺ die, meaning: there is no gloating over death. "You will die, O our Messenger, and they will die." And His words, ﴿Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, you will dispute﴾, mean: believer and disbeliever, strong and weak, all of you will stand before God, and He will judge between you concerning what you used to dispute, both matters of religion and matters of worldly life together.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The legitimacy of presenting examples to greatly enhance understanding and guidance for one who is to be guided.

2- An illustration of the example of the polytheist and the monotheist: the polytheist is in bewilderment and toil, while the monotheist is in ease and tranquillity of mind.

3- Affirmation that every soul shall taste death.

4- An indication that there will be a dispute on the Day of Resurrection, in which God will judge with truth, for He is the Truth.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 39, verses 32–35:

Explanation of the words:

"And who is more unjust than one who lies against Allah?" (Man azlamu mimman kadhaba 'ala Allah?): That is, by attributing to Him what is free of Him, such as a spouse, a child, or a partner.

"And denies the truth when it has come to him?" (Wa kadhaba bi-l-sidqi idh ja'ahu?): That is, the Qur'an, the Prophet, the Oneness of God, the Resurrection, and the recompense.

"An abode for the disbelievers" (mathwan lil-kafirin): That is, a dwelling place, a place of residence and lodging.

"And the one who brought the truth and affirmed it" (Wa alladhi ja'a bi-l-sidqi wa saddaqa bihi): Muhammad (ﷺ), and the one who affirmed it was Abu Bakr and all the Companions of the Messenger of Allah.

"Those are the mindful ones" (Ula'ika hum al-muttaqun): That is, they are safe from the punishment of Allah through their faith and their God-consciousness (taqwa), by abandoning shirk and sins.

"That is the recompense of the good-doers" (Dhalika jaza'u al-muhsinin): That is, the aforementioned bliss of Paradise is the recompense of the good-doers in their deeds.

"That Allah may remove from them the worst of what they did" (Li-yukaffira Allahu 'anhum aswa'a alladhi 'amilu): That is, Allah facilitates this for them and guides them to it, so that He may expiate their sins.

The meaning of the verses:

He, the Exalted, informs His servants, warning and admonishing them, that there is no one more unjust than one who lies against Allah. He says about Him what He has not said, or forbids what He has not forbidden, or permits what He has not permitted, or legislates what He has not legislated, or denies the truth, which is the Qur'an, the Prophet, and the guidance and true religion he brought. So there is no one more unjust than one whose state is this: he lies against Allah and denies the truth.

As for His saying, the Exalted: "Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?" This is a statement of the recompense of the liars and deniers, who are the disbelievers, because of their lying against Allah and their denial of Him. He, the Exalted, affirms that their recompense is lasting residence in Hell. His saying, the Exalted: "And the one who brought the truth and affirmed it, those are the mindful ones" is an announcement of the group of successful servants of Allah, who are the truthful in everything they report, and those who affirm what Allah has made obligatory to affirm. Entering this group primarily are the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, then all the Companions and the believers until the Day of Judgment.

His saying, the Exalted: "Those are the mindful ones" indicates that they guarded against everything that angers Allah, such as shirk and sins, and by this they earned deliverance from the Fire and entry into Paradise, expressed by His saying, the Exalted: "For them is whatever they wish with their Lord" of bliss, some of which has never occurred to anyone's mind, nor has any eye seen it, nor has any ear heard of it.

His saying: "That is the recompense of the good-doers" means: that which was mentioned in His saying "for them is whatever they wish with their Lord" is their recompense and the recompense of all good-doers. The good-doers are those who did good in belief, speech and action. His saying, the Exalted: "That Allah may remove from them the worst of what they did" means: of sins, transgressions, errors and misdeeds; that is, He enabled them to do good and made it easy for them, so that He may expiate for them the worst of what they did and its evil, and recompense them their reward for their faith, their God-consciousness and their goodness in that, with the best of what they used to do, and its goodness as well. The reward is multiplied for them, so that small good deeds are counted like great ones, and the whole recompense becomes according to the best. "What they used to do" is everything Allah legislated for His servants and worshipped them with, including faith and all other acts of obedience and devotion.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Condemnation of lying against Allah the Exalted and of denying Him, and of the religion brought by His Messenger (ﷺ).

2- Explanation of the recompense of those who lie against Allah and of those who deny what the Messenger of Allah brought from Allah of law and religion.

3- Encouragement toward truthfulness in beliefs, speech and actions.

4- The virtue of God-consciousness and goodness, and an explanation of their recompense with Allah on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 39, verses 36–40:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Is not God sufficient for His servant?﴾: Yes, He is sufficient for His servant and messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) in everything that concerns him.

﴿And they threaten you with those besides Him﴾: that is, with the idols and images, that they may afflict you with what distresses and harms you.

﴿Is not God Almighty, Lord of Retribution?﴾: Yes indeed, He is the Almighty, Who prevails over His affair, the Lord of severe retribution against whoever opposes Him.

﴿Surely they will say, "God"﴾: that is, because of the clarity of the proof, the strength of the evidence, and the cutting off of their argument.

﴿Say: "Have you considered?"﴾: that is, tell me.

﴿Can they remove His harm?﴾ ... ﴿Can they withhold His mercy?﴾: The answer is no. So say: "God is sufficient for me; I have no need of anything besides Him."

﴿Act according to your position﴾: that is, according to your state of disbelief and obstinacy.

﴿I am acting﴾: that is, according to my state of faith and submission.

﴿Upon whom will come a punishment that disgraces him﴾: that is, in this world, through killing, captivity, hunger and famine.

﴿And upon whom will descend an enduring punishment﴾: that is, and there will descend upon him a lasting punishment that does not cease, which is the punishment of the Fire after death.

Explanation of the verses:

The context continues to defend the Messenger and to refute his opponents and adversaries, who were slow to see his death. God the Exalted answered them with His saying: ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed they will die﴾ [az-Zumar: 30], so there is no gloating over death. His saying: ﴿Is not God sufficient for His servant?﴾ indicates that the people tried to kill him (ﷺ) when he had not died by his appointed term; they had indeed resolved to kill him and offered rewards to whoever would kill him. In this verse God reassured His Messenger that they would not reach him, and that He is sufficient for him against their plots and threats. So He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Is not God sufficient for His servant?﴾ The answer is yes, since the interrogative is affirmative: He is sufficient for him in everything that concerns him and distresses him. His saying: ﴿And they threaten you with those besides Him﴾ means: and the polytheists threaten you, O our Messenger, with what they worship besides us, of idols and images, that they may afflict you with killing or madness. So do not be concerned by that, for their idols neither harm nor benefit, neither bring nor repel anything. His saying: ﴿And whoever God guides, none can mislead﴾, and your Lord has guided you, so there is none who can mislead you ever; just as whoever God has misled, like your people, has no guide who can guide him ever. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is not God Mighty, Lord of Retribution?﴾ Yes indeed; He will then take vengeance on His enemies for His friends if they persist in harming them, in disbelief and obstinacy, and Glorified and Exalted is He, He has done so.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?"﴾ that is, brought them into being without a prior model ﴿they will surely say, "God."﴾ So since their acknowledgment that God the Exalted is the Creator is binding, why worship other than Him and persist in it, which led them to harm the believers and wage war against them? His saying: ﴿Say: "Have you considered what you invoke besides God?"﴾ that is, the idols and images. Tell me: ﴿If God intends harm for me, can they remove His harm? Or if He intends mercy for me﴾, health, well-being, wealth and victory ﴿can they withhold His mercy?﴾ The answer is no, for they are inanimate objects, unable to give or to withhold. So say: "God is sufficient for me; I worship Him and put my trust in Him," for He is the One who harms and benefits, brings good and repels evil and harm.

His saying: ﴿Upon Him do the trusting put their trust﴾: that is, upon God alone do the trusting place their trust, confident in His sufficiency for them, entrusting their affairs to Him and clinging to Him, and shaking off their hands from others.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "O my people, act according to your position"﴾: that is, since you have refused anything but obstinacy, persisting in polytheism after the proofs and decisive evidence of its falsehood have been established, then act according to your position, that is, your state of polytheism and obstinacy. ﴿I am acting﴾: I am in my state of faith, monotheism and submission. The outcome will become apparent later without doubt, and the truthful will be distinguished from the falsifier, and the guided from the astray. This is His saying, exalted is He:

﴿So you will soon know who will receive a punishment that disgraces him﴾: that is, humbles him and breaks his pride through killing, captivity, hunger and famine. This afflicted the polytheists at Makkah and Badr. His saying: ﴿And upon whom will descend an enduring punishment﴾, which is the punishment of the Fire in the Hereafter. We seek refuge in God from both punishments: the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and the punishment of the Fire in the abode of the Hereafter.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Affirmation of God's sufficiency and His guardianship over His believing servants, especially their leaders among the prophets and the friends of God.

2- Affirmation of what guardianship requires, which is God's vengeance on His enemies for His friends, however long the time.

3- Affirmation of monotheism and refutation of associating rivals with God.

4- Manifestations of God's lordship which necessitate His divinity.

5- The obligation of trusting in God and believing in His sufficiency for His friends.

6- Affirmation of God's fulfilment of His promise to His Messenger and the believers.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 39, verses 41–45:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth﴾: That is, We have sent down to you, O Our Messenger, the Qur'an in truth, meaning accompanied by truth.

﴿And you are not over them a manager﴾: That is, the matter of their guidance is not your responsibility, so that you would compel them to believe.

﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death﴾: That is, He ends the lives of the servants by seizing their souls at the completion of their terms.

﴿And those that have not died during their sleep﴾: That is, He takes them at the time of sleep, withholding them from activity as if they were something seized.

﴿Then He withholds those for which He has decreed death﴾: That is, He seizes them, by a wisdom, with death upon them during sleep.

﴿And sends the others back until a specified term﴾: That is, those for which He has not decreed death He sends back, and their owner lives until the end of the term appointed for him.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought﴾: That is, in the seizing and sending back of souls, and the power to do so, are proofs and evidences of Allah's power over the Resurrection, which the polytheists denied.

﴿Or have they taken other than Allah as intercessors?﴾: That is, the disbelievers of Makkah do not reflect, and if they had reflected they would not have denied the Resurrection, nor would they have taken other than Allah as intercessors, because the falsehood of that is clear.

﴿Say: Even though they do not possess anything and do not reason?﴾: That is, say to them: Will your partners intercede for you even though they possess nothing, denying them the claim of intercession for you? They are idols that neither possess nor reason.

﴿Say: To Allah belongs all intercession﴾: That is, inform them that all intercession belongs to Allah alone. The intercession of the prophets, the martyrs, the scholars and the children is owned by Allah, so no one intercedes except by His permission.

﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink﴾: That is, when Allah alone is mentioned, as when the Messenger ﷺ said "There is no god but Allah," the souls of the polytheists are repulsed and constricted, and anger and displeasure appear on their faces.

﴿But when those other than Him are mentioned﴾: That is, the idols and images they worship besides Allah.

﴿Immediately they rejoice﴾: That is, they are glad and delighted, because they are infatuated with their idols and have forgotten the right of Allah the Exalted over them, which is worshipping Him alone in return for His creating, providing for them, and arranging their lives.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context was about the ongoing conflict between the Messenger ﷺ and his polytheist people. Allah defended His Messenger, repelled from him every harm and hardship, and threatened his opponents with punishment in this world and the Hereafter. Here He consoles and strengthens him, saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book﴾, that is the Qur'an, ﴿for the people﴾, that is for guiding and reforming people, ﴿in truth﴾, that is accompanied by truth. Whoever is guided by the Qur'an, believes and does righteous deeds, the benefit returns to him, as he is saved from the Fire and enters Paradise. Whoever goes astray by not accepting the guidance of the Qur'an, persists in polytheism and sins, then he only goes astray to his own detriment, that is, the harm of his error returns upon himself, for he is the one who is deprived of Paradise and the pleasure of Allah, and is cast into the Fire to abide therein forever, with the wrath of Allah upon him that never leaves him.

And His saying: ﴿And you are not over them a manager﴾, that is, the matter of their guidance has not been entrusted to you, so do not find yourself distressed over it. Your duty is only to convey the clear message. You have not been charged with guarding their deeds or calling them to account for them, nor with the matter of their guidance so that you would compel them to it.

And the Exalted's saying, in the second verse of this context [42]: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death﴾, that is, He seizes their spirits ﴿at the time of their death﴾, that is at the end of their term. He commands the Angel of Death, who brings out the spirit by Allah's permission and seizes it. ﴿And those that have not died during their sleep﴾, that is He seizes them, meaning He withholds them from activity during sleep. If He wills their death, He keeps them and does not return them to their bodies; and if He does not will their death, He releases them, so they return to the body and their owner lives until the appointed term for him, which is the end of his life. Indeed in that seizing and releasing of the spirit, and in death and life, are signs, that is proofs and arguments, all of which decisively show that the One Who is able to do this is able to resurrect and raise up, which the polytheists denied. Just as the possessor of this great power is the possessor of absolute right to obedience and worship, and worship is not fitting except to Him. And His saying ﴿for a people who give thought﴾ refers to those who are alive through faith. As for the dead, who are the disbelievers, they find in this neither sign nor proof, because they have died through polytheism and disbelief.

And the Exalted's saying, in the third verse [43]: ﴿Or have they taken other than Allah as intercessors?﴾, that is, rather, the polytheists, who were expected to be guided by the decisive proofs and clear evidences had they reflected, instead of being guided to the Oneness of Allah, took beside Him idols they named intercessors, hoping for their intercession with Allah to fulfil their needs. This was due to their ignorance and feebleness of intellect. Allah said to His Messenger: ﴿Say: Even though they do not possess anything and do not reason?﴾, that is, say to them: Will they intercede for you even though they possess nothing of the means of intercession and its requirements, and even though they do not understand the meaning of intercession nor comprehend it, because they are idols and stones? The interrogation is for rebuke and reproach. If only the people knew. Then Allah commanded His Messenger to announce the truth, even though it is bitter to the polytheists: ﴿Say: To Allah belongs all intercession﴾, that is all kinds of intercession belong to Allah and are specific to Him, so no one intercedes except by His permission. Therefore, seek intercession from its Owner, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, not from one who is owned by Him. And His saying ﴿Then to Him you will be returned﴾, that is after death, whether you like it or not. So take for yourselves a hand with Him through faith in Him and by making Him alone the object of worship.

And the Exalted's saying: ﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink﴾. This reveals the condition of the polytheists and their ignorance and folly: when they hear "There is no god but Allah," they recoil and constrict, and this appears as anger in their faces; they almost lash out at whoever says "There is no god but Allah." ﴿But when those other than Him are mentioned﴾, that is, when the idols they worship besides Allah are mentioned, ﴿immediately they rejoice﴾, glad and pleased. This is due to their infatuation with their idols and their forgetting the rights of their Lord over them, which are faith in Him and worshipping Him alone, in return for His creating them, providing for them, and arranging their lives. But how can people of darkened souls and inverted hearts understand and comprehend?

Guidance from the verses:

1- The consolation of the Messenger ﷺ and his being empowered to be patient and steadfast in the most difficult circumstances.

2- Manifestations of Allah's power in death and life, which demand faith in Him, in meeting Him, and in His Oneness.

3- Refutation of the polytheists' argument for worshipping idols for the sake of intercession, since all intercession belongs to Allah.

4- Clarification of the error of one who seeks intercession from other than Allah, since none possesses intercession but Him.

5- Demonstration of the folly and misguidance of the polytheists in their anger when hearing monotheism and their joy when hearing polytheism.

This reveals the condition of the polytheists and their ignorance and folly: when they hear "There is no god but Allah," they recoil and constrict, and this appears as anger in their faces; they almost lash out at whoever says "There is no god but Allah." ﴿But when those other than Him are mentioned﴾, that is, when the idols they worship besides Allah are mentioned, ﴿immediately they rejoice﴾, glad and pleased. 1- The consolation of the Messenger ﷺ and his being empowered to be patient and steadfast in the most difficult circumstances.

2- Manifestations of Allah's power in death and life, which demand faith in Him, in meeting Him, and in His Oneness.

3- Refutation of the polytheists' argument for worshipping idols for the sake of intercession, since all intercession belongs to Allah.

4- Clarification of the error of one who seeks intercession from other than Allah, since none possesses intercession but Him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 39, verses 49–52:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Fa-idha massa al-insana durrun da'anaa﴾: That is, if harm befalls the disbelieving human being, such as sickness or anything else that harms him, he calls upon Us, that is, he asks Us to remove his harm.

﴿Thumma idha khawwalnahu ni'matan minna﴾: Then, when We bestow upon him a blessing from Us, that is, health, wealth, or other things.

﴿Qala innama utitahu ala 'ilm﴾: He says, that is, that disbeliever says: "I was only given this provision on account of knowledge from God that I deserve it."

﴿Bal hiya fitnah﴾: That blessing was not given to him because of his worthiness for it; rather, it was given as a trial and a test for him.

﴿Wa lakinna aktharahum la ya'lamun﴾: That is, what they are given of wealth, health and well-being is a trial for them and not a sign of God's pleasure with them.

﴿Qad qalaha alladhina min qablihim﴾: That is, those who came before them said the same words, such as Qarun, so they did not remain long before they were seized. "What they used to earn did not avail them."

﴿Wa alladhina zalamu min ha'ulai sayusibuhum﴾: That is, those among these who wronged by associating partners with God, that is, the disbelievers of Quraysh, will also be struck.

﴿Sayyi'atu ma kasabu﴾: As those before them were struck, and they were struck by a seven-year famine and were killed at Badr.

﴿Wa ma hum bi-mu'jizin﴾: That is, they will not escape God nor overpower Him.

﴿Awa lam ya'lamu anna Allaha yabsutu al-rizqa﴾: That is, they said that statement and did not know that God expands provision.

﴿Liman yasha'u wa yaqdiru﴾: That is, He expands it for whomever He wills as a test, and constricts it as a trial.

﴿Inna fi dhalika la-ayatin li-qawmin yu'minun﴾: That is, in that mentioned expansion as a test and constriction as a trial are signs, that is, indications of God's power and the perfection of His management of the affairs of His creation.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to describe the bewilderment of the polytheists and the corruption of their hearts as a result of their disbelief and ignorance. His words, exalted is He, ﴿Fa-idha massa al-insana durrun da'anaa﴾ refer to that disbeliever who, when God alone is mentioned, his soul recoils, and when the idols are mentioned, he is delighted and rejoices. When this human being is touched by harm, such as sickness or other things that harm and do not please him, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance, and associates no one with Him in this state, knowing that idols neither remove harm nor give good. When God bestows upon him a blessing from His grace as a trial, he says: "I was given what I was given on account of knowledge from God that I am worthy of it." God refutes him, saying: ﴿Bal hiya fitnah﴾, "Rather, it is a trial." ﴿Wa lakinna aktharahum la ya'lamun﴾, but most of them, that is, most of the polytheists, do not know that when God gives them, He gives them only to test them, not out of love for them nor out of His pleasure with them. The evidence that this provision for the polytheists is only a trial is that this statement of theirs was said by those before them, such as Qarun and others, and they did not remain long before God seized them for their sins, and what they used to earn of vast wealth did not avail them. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Fa-asabahum sayyi'atu ma kasabu﴾, so they were not seized without sin; rather, they were seized for their sins. This is His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Fa-asabahum sayyi'atu ma kasabu﴾, and His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Wa alladhina zalamu min ha'ulai﴾, that is, from the disbelievers of Quraysh, ﴿sayusibuhum﴾ also will strike them: the evil deeds of what they earned through polytheism, obstinacy and wrongdoing. ﴿Wa ma hum bi-mu'jizin﴾, and they will never escape God, for how could they, when a seven-year famine struck them, and they were killed and captured at Badr and at the Conquest?

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Awa lam ya'lamu anna Allaha yabsutu al-rizqa liman yasha'u wa yaqdir﴾: that is, they said their statement and did not know that God expands provision for whomever He wills as a test for him, whether he will be grateful or disbelieve, and constricts it for whomever He wills as a trial for him, whether he will be patient or fret and become wrathful. Thus His expansion of provision is not out of love for the one given abundance, nor is His constriction out of hatred for the one restricted. Rather, expansion and constriction alike serve the wisdom of training and management. But the disbelievers do not know this, and their ignorance of the wisdom has led them to say falsehood and believe in it. As for the believers, they do not say their statement, because of their knowledge and the light of their hearts. Therefore they find the signs in such management clear, indicating God's knowledge, wisdom and power, and so their faith, light and insight increase.

Guidance of the verses:

1- Demonstration of the contradiction of the people of disbelief, ignorance and error throughout their lives, for they live in the darkness of ignorance and disbelief.

2- Affirmation that no calamity befalls except because of a sin, whether evident or hidden, great or small.

3- Explanation that the expansion and constriction of provision for individuals or groups does not reflect God's love or hatred for the servant, but returns to the laws of divine training and the wisdom of managing the affairs of creation.

4- The people of faith are those who benefit from the signs and proofs, for they are living, seeing and understanding; as for the people of disbelief, they are dead, not seeing the signs nor understanding them.

5- God's threat to wrongdoers and His severe warning that He will strike them as He struck others, as recompense for their wrongdoing and corrupt earnings.
