Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 39, verses 53–59:

Explanation of the words:

"O My servants who have transgressed against themselves": that is, who have gone to excess in harming themselves by committing sins.

"Do not despair of the mercy of Allah": that is, do not despair of His forgiveness for you and of your entry into Paradise.

"Indeed, Allah forgives all sins": that is, the sins of one who associates partners with Allah and who commits immorality, if he repents with sincere repentance (tawbah nasuh).

"And turn back in repentance to your Lord": that is, return to Him through faith and obedience.

"And submit to Him": that is, make your deeds sincerely for Him.

"And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord": that is, the Noble Qur'an, so that you make lawful what it has made lawful and unlawful what it has made unlawful.

"Lest a soul should say, 'Oh, my regret'": that is, the soul of the disbeliever and the criminal says, "Oh, my regret," meaning, "Oh, my remorse."

"Over what I neglected in regard to Allah": that is, concerning the right of Allah, so that I did not obey Him as others obeyed Him.

"And indeed, I was among the mockers": that is, among those who ridiculed the religion of Allah the Exalted and His believing servants.

"If only I had another turn, I would be among the doers of good": that is, if only I had a return to the worldly life, I would then be among the believers who perfected their intention and their deeds.

"Yes, but My verses had come to you": that is, the matter is not as you claim, that you wish for guidance; rather, My verses came to you, but you denied them and became arrogant.

Meaning of the verses:

It is established that some people had associated partners with Allah, killed, and committed adultery, and this weighed heavily upon them. They said, "Let us send someone to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to ask him whether there is any repentance for us. If he says yes, well and good; otherwise we will remain as we are." Before their messenger arrived, this verse was revealed: "Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves" — that is, who have gone to excess in committing crimes, thereby being wasteful toward their own souls — "do not despair" — that is, do not lose hope — "of the mercy of Allah," that He will forgive your sins and admit you to Paradise, if you repent to Him and turn back to Him. "Indeed, Allah forgives all sins" — for whoever repents from them — for nothing is beyond His power so that He could not forgive it or refrain from punishing for it; "indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful."

And the saying of Allah the Exalted: "And turn back in repentance to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you, and then you will not be helped" — that is, O sinners who have gone to excess, turn back to your Lord, that is, return to His obedience by doing what is commanded and abandoning what is forbidden. "And submit to Him" — that is, make your deeds sincere for Him, outwardly and inwardly, hastening thereby before the punishment descends upon you. "Then you will not be helped" — that is, you will not be able to prevent it from you or repel it from you.

"And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord" — in this mighty Qur'an. So comply with the command, avoid the prohibition, hold to the firm obligations, and leave aside the dispensations, also hastening before the punishment descends upon you "suddenly," that is, unexpectedly, while you are not aware of it. Hasten to repentance, turning back, and sincere submission, before a time when the soul says, "Oh, my regret, oh, my remorse," which brings me grief and sorrow. "Be present, this is the time of your presence" over my neglect in regard to the right of Allah the Exalted, in that I did not worship Him with the worship due to Him, nor remembered Him, nor thanked Him. "And indeed, I was among the mockers" — that is, those who ridiculed His religion and His believing servants. What a confession that will bring its owner into the midst of Hellfire! Hasten, O servants of Allah, to this and that.

"Or [lest] it say, 'If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous.' Or [lest] it say when it sees the punishment, 'If only I had another turn, so I could be among the doers of good.'" — that is, a return to the life of this world.

Allah the Exalted said, refuting their false wishes: "Yes" — that is, the matter is not as you claimed, O one who wishes by your saying, "If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous," [guarding] against shirk and the sins into which you fell and into Hell. Rather, My verses came to you, guiding and showing you the way, but you denied them and were arrogant toward acting upon what came in them, and you were among the disbelievers in that.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1. The explanation of Allah's grace and mercy toward His servants, in accepting the repentance of a servant if he repents, however great his sins.

2. The call of the Merciful Lord to His sinful servants: to turn back to Him and to submit sincerely to Him.

3. The affirmation of resurrection and recompense by mentioning what happens therein and the terrors that take place in its courtyard.

4. The obligation to hasten repentance and to rush to it before punishment descends in this world or death comes, for death is more grievous and bitter, since repentance is never accepted after death.

5. The encouragement to take up the firm obligations and to leave the dispensations without necessity.

6. The refutation of the doctrine of the Jabriyyah (fatalists), who hold that they are compelled to commit sins and to fall into transgressions, like the saying of one of them: "If only Allah had guided me, I would have done such-and-such or left such-and-such."

7. The virtue of piety (taqwa) and excellence (ihsan), and the excellence of the pious and the doers of good.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 39, verses 60–66:

Explanation of the words:

"And on the Day of Resurrection": that is, when people are raised from their graves.

"You will see those who lied against Allah": that is, by taking protectors other than Him and by speaking falsehood about Him, glory be to Him and exalted.

"Their faces will be blackened": that is, black with distress and grief, and a sign that they are among the people of the Fire and that they were among those who lied against their Lord.

"Is there not in Hell a dwelling for the arrogant?": that is, is there not in Hell an abode and a dwelling place for the arrogant? Yes indeed, for them therein is a dwelling, wretched is that dwelling for the arrogant who turned away from the worship of Allah, exalted is He.

"And Allah will save those who feared Him": that is, He will save them from the Fire because of their taqwa (God-consciousness) and their avoidance of shirk and sins.

"With their triumph, no evil will touch them, nor will they grieve": that is, by their success in attaining Paradise and their entry into it, no evil, meaning punishment, will touch them, nor will they grieve over what they have attained of bliss.

"To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth": that is, the keys to the treasuries of the heavens and the earth.

"Those are the losers": that is, the losers with respect to themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection.

"Say: Do you order me to worship other than Allah?": say, O Messenger, to those who asked you to worship alongside their gods: do you order me to worship other than Allah? Is worship fit for other than Him, when He is the Lord and God of everything? How wretched is your understanding, O ignorant ones.

"Even if you associate [with Allah], your deeds will surely be lost": that is, by way of supposition, if you were to associate another with Allah in His worship, your deeds would be nullified, and you would be among the losers.

"Rather, worship Allah and be among the thankful": that is, rather, I worship Allah alone, since none deserves worship but Him, and be among those who thank Him for His favour upon you through prophethood, messengership, protection and guidance.

Meaning of the verses:

Earlier in the context, there was a command to hasten repentance before death, lest the opportunity be lost. This is because the Day of Resurrection is a day of terrors and changing conditions, and the two following verses explain this. Allah, the Exalted, says: "And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied against Allah" by attributing to Him offspring, partners, and permitting and forbidding, when He is free of all that. "Their faces will be blackened" as a sign that they disbelieved, lied, and are among the people of the Fire.

His saying, exalted is He: "Is there not in Hell a dwelling for the arrogant?" means: yes indeed, in Hell is an abode and dwelling place for those who were arrogant toward faith and worship. His saying, exalted is He: "And Allah will save..." means: that is one state, and this is another, namely that Allah, the Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection will save those who guarded against shirk and sins through faith and obedience. These, by their triumph into Paradise, no evil will touch them in the places of the Resurrection, nor will they grieve over what they left behind in the world, because the bliss of Paradise that they attained makes them forget what they left behind. His saying, exalted is He: "Allah is the Creator of all things" means: there is no existent other than Allah except that it is created and Allah is its Creator. "And He is, over all things, Disposer of affairs" means: Guardian and Protector. Glory be to Him, how great is His power and how vast His knowledge; therefore worship is due to Him, and it is not permitted to be directed to anyone else, let alone to be obligatory for anyone else.

His saying, exalted is He: "To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth" means: truly, to Him belong the keys to the treasuries of mercy, goodness and blessings. He opens what He wills and withholds what He wills, so requests are valid only to Him and desire is permissible only for Him. People worship idols and statues only out of desire and fear; if they knew that fear is only directed to the One who has power over everything, and that desire is only directed to the One in whose hand is everything, they would never have worshipped anyone other than Allah in any way.

His saying, exalted is He: "And those who disbelieved in the signs of Allah," which contain His faith, His attributes, the clarification of what He loves and dislikes, His limits and His laws. Whoever disbelieves in the signs of Allah, not believing in them and not acting upon what they contain, loses a clear loss, such that on the Day of Resurrection he loses himself and his family; and that is the manifest loss.

His saying, exalted is He: "Say: Do you order me..." The verse is a response to the polytheists who asked the Messenger to acknowledge their gods and be content with them in exchange for their acknowledging what he brought and calling to it. So Allah commanded him to break off with them by saying: "Do you order me to worship other than Allah, O ignorant ones?" This will never be from me, ever. How could I worship other than Allah when He is my Lord and the Master of my affair, and He is the One who honoured me with knowledge of Him and revealed His laws to me? So let them despair, for such a thing will never happen. He described them as ignorant because their ignorance of Allah and His greatness is what embellished for them the worship of other than Him and zealotry for it.

His saying, exalted is He: "And it has already been revealed to you," meaning Allah revealed to you, as He revealed to the prophets before you, the following, by the might and majesty of Allah: "If you associate [with Allah]," by Our reckoning, not in Our worship, "your deeds will surely be lost," meaning all of it will be nullified and you will not be rewarded for any of it, however little; and you will certainly be among the losers, who lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection, and that is the manifest loss. Then Allah commanded His Messenger, affirming monotheism and nullifying shirk, by saying: "Rather, worship Allah and be among the thankful," meaning: Allah alone, so worship Him and be among those who thank Him for His favour and bounty upon you.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The blackening of faces on the Day of Resurrection is a sign of disbelief and of eternal abiding in Hell.

2- The whitening of faces on the Day of Resurrection is a sign of faith and of eternal abiding in Paradise.

3- Affirmation of the Resurrection and the recompense by describing its conditions and what takes place in it.

4- All things are in Allah's hand, so it is never valid to seek anything from other than Him; whoever seeks something from other than Allah is among the most ignorant of creatures.

5- Condemnation of shirk and clarification of its gravity, for it nullifies deeds entirely.

6- The obligation to worship Allah by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, and the obligation to praise and thank Him, since every favour is from Him and every bounty is His. So to Allah belong praise and grace.

He opens what He wills and withholds what He wills, so requests are valid only to Him and desire is permissible only for Him. People worship idols and statues only out of desire and fear; if they knew that fear is only directed to the One who has power over everything, and that desire is only directed to the One in whose hand is everything, they would never have worshipped anyone other than Allah in any way.

His saying, exalted is He: "And those who disbelieved in the signs of Allah," which contain His faith, His attributes, the clarification of what He loves and dislikes, His limits and His laws. Whoever disbelieves in the signs of Allah, not believing in them and not acting upon what they contain, loses a clear loss, such that on the Day of Resurrection he loses himself and his family; and that is the manifest loss.

His saying, exalted is He: "Say: Do you order me..." The verse is a response to the polytheists who asked the Messenger to acknowledge their gods and be content with them in exchange for their acknowledging what he brought and calling to it. So Allah commanded him to break off with them by saying: "Do you order me to worship other than Allah, O ignorant ones?" This will never be from me, ever. How could I worship other than Allah when He is my Lord and the Master of my affair, and He is the One who honoured me with knowledge of Him and revealed His laws to me? So let them despair, for such a thing will never happen. He described them as ignorant because their ignorance of Allah and His greatness is what embellished for them the worship of other than Him and zealotry for it.

His saying, exalted is He: "And it has already been revealed to you," meaning Allah revealed to you, as He revealed to the prophets before you, the following, by the might and majesty of Allah: "If you associate [with Allah]," by Our reckoning, not in Our worship, "your deeds will surely be lost," meaning all of it will be nullified and you will not be rewarded for any of it, however little; and you will certainly be among the losers, who lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection, and that is the manifest loss. Then Allah commanded His Messenger, affirming monotheism and nullifying shirk, by saying: "Rather, worship Allah and be among the thankful," meaning: Allah alone, so worship Him and be among those who thank Him for His favour and bounty upon you.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The blackening of faces on the Day of Resurrection is a sign of disbelief and of eternal abiding in Hell.

2- The whitening of faces on the Day of Resurrection is a sign of faith and of eternal abiding in Paradise.

3- Affirmation of the Resurrection and the recompense by describing its conditions and what takes place in it.

4- All things are in Allah's hand, so it is never valid to seek anything from other than Him; whoever seeks something from other than Allah is among the most ignorant of creatures.

5- Condemnation of shirk and clarification of its gravity, for it nullifies deeds entirely.

6- The obligation to worship Allah by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, and the obligation to praise and thank Him, since every favour is from Him and every bounty is His. So to Allah belong praise and grace.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 39, verses 67–70:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Wa-ma qadarū Allāh ḥaqqa qadrihi﴾ (They did not measure God with the true measure of His greatness): That is, they did not magnify God with the true magnitude of His greatness, nor did they know Him with the true knowledge of Him, when they associated with His worship others, their idols.

﴿Wal-arḍu jamī'an qabḍatuhu﴾ (The earth entirely in His grasp): That is, the earth with all its parts is in His grasp.

﴿Wal-samāwātu maṭwiyyātun biyamīnihi﴾ (And the heavens folded up in His right hand): That is, the seven heavens are folded up in His right hand.

﴿Subḥānahu wa-ta'ālā 'ammā yushrikūn﴾ (Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him): That is, He is holy and free from what the polytheists associate with Him of idols.

﴿Wa-nufikha fī al-ṣūr﴾ (And the Horn will be blown): That is, Isrāfīl blows the blast of swooning.

﴿Thumma nufikha fīhi ukhrā﴾ (Then it will be blown again): That is, another time, and this is the blast of standing up before the Lord of the worlds.

﴿Wa-ashraqati al-arḍu bi-nūri rabbihā﴾ (And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord): That is, the earth will be illuminated with the light of God, Exalted, when He manifests Himself to judge.

﴿Wa-wuḍi'a al-kitāb﴾ (And the Book will be placed): That is, the book of deeds, for the reckoning.

﴿Wa-jī'a bil-nabiyyīn wal-shuhadā'﴾ (And the prophets and the witnesses will be brought): That is, the prophets will be brought to bear witness against their nations, and the witnesses are Muhammad (ﷺ) and his community.

﴿Wa-quḍiya baynahum bil-ḥaqq﴾ (And judgment will be made between them with truth): That is, with justice, and they will not be wronged, neither by a diminishing of their good deeds nor by an increase of their evil deeds.

﴿Wa-huwa a'lamu bimā yaf'alūn﴾ (And He is most knowing of what they do): That is, He knows better even than the doers themselves.

Explanation of the verses:

Concerning His saying, ﴿They did not measure God with the true measure of His greatness﴾: After He established Monotheism and condemned polytheism and the polytheists, He informed, rebuking the polytheists for their polytheism and for their calling His Prophet to polytheism, that by their action they did not measure God with the true measure of His greatness; that is, they did not magnify Him with the true magnitude of His greatness, owing to their ignorance of Him when they worshipped others alongside Him and called His Prophet to that. And His saying, ﴿The earth entirely in His grasp on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens folded up in His right hand﴾: He who makes the earth with all its layers and parts in His grasp, and folds the heavens in His right hand, so the heavens and the earth are all in His hand, and He says, "I am the King; where are the kings?" The possessor of this supreme power, how can others be worshipped with Him, which are idols and images and statues? Therefore He declared Himself free of all this by saying ﴿Glory be to Him﴾, that is, He is exalted and holy above partner, equal, consort, child, and the attributes of created things, and ﴿exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾, that is, He is raised above having any partner, and He is the Lord and Owner of everything.

His saying, ﴿And the Horn will be blown﴾ and the verse that follows: This is a presentation of the manifestations of power with which the existence of anyone deserving worship alongside Him, may He be glorified and exalted, is rationally incompatible. The one who blows the Horn, that is, the trumpet, is definitely Isrāfīl, for he is the one charged with blowing the Horn. When he blows this blast, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth swoons, except whom God wills. This exception indicates that some of the created beings will not swoon at this blast. ﴿Then it will be blown again﴾, that is, into the Horn, another blast, ﴿and behold, they will be standing, looking on﴾. This blast is called the blast of standing up before the Lord of the worlds, for the sake of the reckoning. And His saying, ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the Book will be placed﴾: that is, the book of deeds for the reckoning. ﴿And the prophets will be brought﴾ to bear witness against their nations, and the witnesses will be brought, and they are the community of Muhammad, who will bear witness over the earlier nations that their messengers had conveyed to them the call of God. The testimony of the community of Muhammad rests on what God, Exalted, has informed them of in His Book, the Noble Qur'an, that the messengers conveyed the messages of their Lord to their nations. This is supported by His saying, ﴿And thus We have made you a middle nation﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143], that is, excellent and upright, ﴿that you may be witnesses over mankind, and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. And His saying, ﴿And judgment will be made between them with truth﴾: that is, God, Exalted, judges among the servants with justice, and every soul is paid in full for what it did of good or evil. He, Exalted, is most knowing of what they do, even more than the doers themselves. Therefore the reckoning will be just, with no injustice in it, for it is free of error, mistake, ignorance and forgetfulness, the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, being exalted above all that.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Demonstration of the manifestations of the Lord's greatness, with which associating others with Him in worship, Mighty and Majestic, is incompatible.

2- Affirmation of the Resurrection and recompense, describing its conditions and what takes place.

3- Demonstration of God's justice in His judgment among His servants on the plains of Resurrection.

4- The excellence of this community in being accepted as witnesses over the nations that preceded it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 39, verses 71–75:

Explanation of the words:

Wa-suqa alladhina kafaru (﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven﴾): that is, the angels drive those who disbelieved with violence.

Ila Jahannama zumaran (﴿to Hell in groups﴾): that is, in companies: the company of the polytheists, the company of the criminals, and the company of the wrongdoers.

Wa-qala lahum khazanatuha (﴿and its keepers will say to them﴾): that is, those entrusted with the Fire from among the angels; the singular is khazin (keeper).

Alam ya'tikum rusul (﴿Did there not come to you messengers﴾): this interrogative is for affirmation and rebuke.

Haqqat kalimat al-'adhab (﴿the word of punishment has come into effect﴾): that is, the punishment became obligatory upon the disbelievers.

Wa-suqa alladhina ittaqaw (﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven﴾): that is, the angels drive, with gentleness, upon noble mounts, those who feared their Lord, meaning they obeyed Him and did not associate partners with Him.

Wa-futihat abwabuha (﴿and its gates will be opened﴾): that is, while the gates of Paradise have already been opened to receive them.

Wal-hamdu lillahi alladhi sadaqana wa'dahu (﴿Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us﴾): that is, He has fulfilled for us His promise of Paradise.

Wa-awrathana al-ard (﴿and has made us inherit the land﴾): that is, the land of Paradise. The form of inheritance is in view of His words, may He be exalted, in His promise to them: ﴿That is the Paradise which We cause to inherit from Our servants those who were devout﴾.

Wa-suqa alladhina ittaqaw (﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven﴾): that is, the angels drive, with gentleness, upon noble mounts, those who feared their Lord, meaning they obeyed Him and did not associate partners with Him.

Wa-futihat abwabuha (﴿and its gates will be opened﴾): that is, while the gates of Paradise have already been opened to receive them.

Wal-hamdu lillahi alladhi sadaqana wa'dahu (﴿Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us﴾): that is, He has fulfilled for us His promise of Paradise.

Wa-awrathana al-ard (﴿and has made us inherit the land﴾): that is, the land of Paradise. The form of inheritance is in view of His words, may He be exalted, in His promise to them: ﴿That is the Paradise which We cause to inherit from Our servants those who were devout﴾.

Natabawwa'u min al-jannati haythu nasha' (﴿We may dwell in Paradise wherever we will﴾): that is, we may settle wherever we wish.

Fa-ni'ma ajru al-'amilin (﴿How excellent is the reward of the workers﴾): that is, Paradise.

Hafffina min hawli al-'arsh (﴿Surrounding the Throne﴾): that is, encircling the Throne from every side.

Yusabbihuna bihamdi rabbihim (﴿glorifying the praise of their Lord﴾): that is, they say, "Glory be to Allah and by His praise."

Wa-qudiya baynahum bil-haqq (﴿And it will be judged between them in truth﴾): that is, Allah judges among all creatures with justice.

Wa-qila al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-'alamin (﴿And it will be said, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾): that is, the angels and the believers will say, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds," upon the settling of the people of Paradise in Paradise and the people of the Fire in the Fire.

Meaning of the verses:

After the conclusion of the judgment upon the people of the standing place, in which Allah judged among them according to their deeds, repaying each doer for his deed, whether disbelief and disobedience or faith and obedience, Allah, exalted, says, reporting the destiny of the two groups: ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups﴾, that is, the angels will drive them with severity and violence because they do not wish to go. ﴿In groups﴾: the word zumra is derived from zamr, which is sound, since a group usually has a sound. His words, ﴿until when they reach it, its gates will be opened﴾: since they were closed like the doors of prisons, which are not opened except when prisoners arrive. ﴿And its keepers will say to them﴾ before they arrive, rebuking them: ﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among you reciting to you the verses of your Lord﴾, that is, clarifying for you guidance from error and truth from falsehood, and what your Lord loves of beliefs, statements, deeds, attributes and essences, and what He dislikes of that, and calling you to do what is loved and to abandon what is hated, so that you may be saved and attain felicity. They will answer, "Yes," that is, they came to us with what you said, "but the word of punishment has come into effect upon the disbelievers, and we are among them, so the punishment became due to us." Then the angels will say to them, ﴿Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein eternally. Wretched is the abode of the arrogant﴾, that is, wretched is the dwelling of the arrogant in Hell as a dwelling.

His words, ﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise﴾: their driving is the driving of noble mounts which they ride, a driving of gentleness and honor to Paradise, the abode of peace, in groups: the group of jihad, the group of charity, the group of scholars, the group of prayers.... ﴿Until when they reach it﴾, and its gates have already been opened to receive them, honored and esteemed, their keepers will say to them, "Peace be upon you; you are good, so enter it," that is, your souls were made good by your good deeds, so your station in the abode of peace became good. How excellent is this greeting, offered in contrast to the reproach and rebuke of the guardians to the people of the Fire.

His words, "Enter it," that is, Paradise, with your eternal abiding decreed for you therein. They will say, after entering Paradise and settling in its palaces: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us﴾, referring to His words: ﴿That is the Paradise which We cause to inherit from Our servants those who were devout﴾ [Maryam: 63]. And their words, ﴿and has made us inherit the land﴾, that is, the land of Paradise, ﴿we may dwell in it wherever we will﴾, that is, we may descend in it wherever we wish to descend. In their words "has made us inherit the land" there is an indication that they inherited it from their two parents, Adam and Eve, since it was theirs before the two descended from it. Their words, ﴿How excellent is the reward of the workers﴾, that is, Paradise; and the intended work is faith and piety in the world through performing the obligations and avoiding the prohibitions. His words, may He be exalted, ﴿And you will see the angels﴾, O seer, ﴿surrounding the Throne﴾, that is, encircling the Throne of the Merciful, that is, His seat, ﴿glorifying the praise of their Lord﴾, that is, saying, "Glory be to Allah and by His praise; glory be to Allah the Mighty." Allah, exalted, says, reporting the end of the standing: ﴿And it will be judged between them in truth﴾, that is, Allah judged among creatures with justice. When the people of the Fire and the people of Paradise had settled, Allah was praised for the complete settling and the just, merciful judgment. ﴿And it will be said, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾, that is, the angels praised their Lord, and the believers praised Him with them while they are in the abode of lasting bliss.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Demonstration of the humiliation of the people of the Fire, by driving them upon their feet with violence and by reproaching and rebuking them.

2- Condemnation of arrogance against worshipping Allah, the Exalted, and against the worship of the believers in Him, who are God-fearing.

3- Demonstration of Allah's honoring of His friends, who are carried upon noble mounts whose saddles are of gold to Paradise, and are met there with greeting and peace: a greeting of respect and honor, and peace, a security from every hated thing.

4- Demonstration of the end of the standing: the settling of the disbelievers and the wicked in the Fire, and the settling of the God-fearing righteous believers in Paradise, the abode of the righteous.

5- Concluding every deed with praise: Allah the Creator began with praise, saying, "Praise be to Allah who created the heavens and the earth," and concluded with praise, saying, "And it will be said, 'Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'"
